Then the row-by-row pair bits of the list made of the literals of $C$, each with clause index $0$, followed by $O_\varphi$, are the rows pushed for the literals of $C$ walked above a clause marker and the items of $\varphi$,…
nodes.title: Pair bits of a leading clause

nodes.summary: For a literal $(x, p)$ with variable index $x \in \mathbb{N}$ and polarity $p$, the token list is the polarity marker symbol for $p$ followed by one name-bit symbol for each bit of the canonical binary representation of $x$ (least significant bit first, empty for $x = 0$), in order.
nodes.title: Polarity-first tokens of a literal

nodes.summary: A symbol is a token of the walk between the stacks $D$ and $E$ when it is a name bit, a literal marker or a clause marker; the value symbols and the dead symbol are not.
nodes.title: Tokens moved by the walk

nodes.summary: An item of the stack $D$ is either $\mathrm{none}$, standing for a clause marker, or an occurrence $(x, p)$ of the variable $x$ with polarity $p$. The tokens of $\mathrm{none}$ are the single clause-marker symbol; the tokens of $(x, p)$ are the polarity marker of $p$ followed by the binary encoding of $x$ as name-bit symbols.
nodes.title: Tokens of an item on the walked stack

nodes.summary: For a CNF formula $\varphi$ with clauses $C_1, \dots, C_m$ in order, the items of $\varphi$ are the list made of, for each $i = 1, \dots, m$ in turn, the literals of $C_i$ in order, each as an occurrence item, followed by one clause-marker item $\mathrm{none}$. These are the items on the stack $D$ once the clauses of $\varphi$ are walked.
nodes.title: Walked items of a formula

nodes.summary: The emitter has nine stacks: $T$ (tokens), $O$ (output), $A$ (the current name), $B$ (scratch), $D$ (walked occurrences), $E$ (the walk's other side), $X$ (scratch), $C$ (the clause count) and $N$ (the occurrence count).

nodes.summary: For a list $I$ of items and literals $l_1, \dots, l_k$, the rows are the concatenation, for $i = 1, \dots, k$ in turn, of the reverse of the walk bits of $l_i$ with flag false over the items $l_{i+1}, \dots, l_k$ (as occurrence items) followed by $I$. These are the bits pushed when the literals of a clause are walked above the items $I$.

This is the form in which the stacks $A$ and $D$ of the CLIQUE emitter hold variable names.

nodes.summary: For every CNF formula $\varphi$, the row bits of $\varphi$ equal the pair bits of Karp's CLIQUE graph of $\varphi$: with $o_0, \dots, o_{m-1}$ the literal occurrences of $\varphi$, these are, for the pairs $(i, j)$ with $i < j < m$ in encoding order (rows $i$ ascending, and $j$ descending within a row), the bits telling whether $o_i$ and $o_j$ lie in different clauses and are not complementary.

nodes.summary: Let $S$ assign contents to the stacks of the CLIQUE emitter and let $c, n \in \mathbb{N}$. If the scratch stacks $B$ and $X$ are empty and the counters $C$ and $N$ hold exactly $c$ and $n$ clause markers, then $S$ is the standard state whose stacks $T$, $O$, $A$, $D$, $E$ hold what they hold in $S$, whose stacks $B$ and $X$ are empty and whose counters $C$ and $N$ hold $c$ and $n$ clause markers.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
